title: Direct object pronouns
practiceFocus: Answer five questions without repeating the noun

points.title: Say it once, then replace it
points.rule: Me lo llevo from day 12 was one fixed chunk. Now build it from parts. Lo replaces a masculine singular thing, la a feminine singular thing, los and las the plurals. The pronoun goes before a conjugated verb, or attaches to the end of an infinitive. Lo voy a comprar and Voy a comprarlo both mean you are going to buy it.

examples.english: Do you want the coffee? Yes, I want it.

examples.spanish: ¿Tienes la llave? No, no la tengo.
examples.english: Do you have the key? No, I don’t have it.
Do you see the messages? Yes, I see them.
Are you buying the apples? Yes, I am buying them.

grammar.notYet: Indirect object pronouns come on day 18. Combining the two pronouns together waits.

phrases.english: Do you want dessert? Yes, I want it.

phrases.spanish: ¿Tienes mi número? No, no lo tengo.
phrases.english: Do you have my number? No, I don’t have it.

phrases.note: La is a feminine thing already mentioned.

phrases.english: Are you watching the film? I am watching it now.
Can you help me? Yes, I can help you.
phrases.note: Me and te attach the same way.

phrases.spanish: ¿Dónde está mi chaqueta? No la veo.
phrases.english: Where is my jacket? I don’t see it.
I am going to try it on.
I am doing it right now.

lines.speaker: Nuria
lines.english: And the map? Are you bringing it?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: No lo tengo. ¿Lo puedes traer tú?
lines.english: I don’t have it. Can you bring it?

lines.speaker: Nuria
lines.spanish: Sí, lo traigo yo. ¿Compraste el agua?
lines.english: Yes, I will bring it. Did you buy the water?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Todavía no. La compro de camino.
lines.english: Not yet. I will buy it on the way.

practice.title: Answer without the noun
practice.instruction: Ask yourself five yes/no questions about things around you, and answer each one using lo, la, los, or las instead of repeating the noun.
tips: Say the noun’s gender out loud first.
Café is masculine, so lo. Llave is feminine, so la.
